title: Natural short exact Hom sequences for a stupid source tail
statement: Let C be a small category, J a Grothendieck topology and R a sheaf of commutative rings. Let P be a cochain complex of sheaves of R-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], and k an integer with P^n zero for n<k. Let G have P^k in degree k and zero elsewhere, with zero differentials, and let U be the stupid tail: P in degrees at least k+1, zero below, and the inherited differentials. For every chain map f:M to N, the three induced Hom maps Hom(G,f), Hom(P,f), Hom(U,f) [def-pur-hom-complex] are, up to isomorphisms of arrows, the three components of a morphism between two short exact sequences of cochain complexes. No boundedness or quasi-isomorphism assumption is imposed on P, M, N or f.

source.place: Tag 0A8X, Hom products and differential; step 2 of lem-pc-bounded-exact-term-hom-quasi-iso; degreewise split sequence entering Tag 0117

proof.text: Take G and U as in the statement. Extension by zero at degree k and restriction to source degrees at least k+1 give maps Hom(G,M) to Hom(P,M) to Hom(U,M). Internal Homs from all source terms below k are zero.

Check the chain-map identities using d_M h - (-1)^n h d_P. The only possible incoming differential for extension is from P^(k-1), which is zero. The restriction differential uses only p and p+1, both at least k+1 for p in the tail. Split each product into its k factor and its tail factors. This proves degreewise split short exactness and hence short exactness as complexes.

Repeat for N. Postcomposition by f commutes with extension and restriction on every product projection. These three maps form a morphism of the two short exact sequences. The universal product identifications with the named Hom complexes supply the three arrow isomorphisms. No infinite-product exactness is used: the product is separated into two direct factors.

proof_origin.place: The bounded exact-term Hom argument, separated into its single-degree and split-tail calculations

theorem exists_homComplex_stupid_tail_shortExact
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u})
    (P : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj R)) ℤ)
    (k : ℤ) (hbelow : ∀ n : ℤ, n < k → IsZero (P.X n))
    {M N : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj R)) ℤ}
    (f : M ⟶ N) : ∃ S T : ShortComplex (CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u}
        ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj R)) ℤ),
      ∃ φ : S ⟶ T, S.ShortExact ∧ T.ShortExact ∧
        Nonempty (Arrow.mk φ.τ₁ ≅ Arrow.mk (((homComplexFunctor (R := R)).obj
          (op ((HomologicalComplex.single _ (ComplexShape.up ℤ) k).obj
            (P.X k)))).map f)) ∧
        Nonempty (Arrow.mk φ.τ₂ ≅ Arrow.mk
          (((homComplexFunctor (R := R)).obj (op P)).map f)) ∧
        Nonempty (Arrow.mk φ.τ₃ ≅ Arrow.mk (((homComplexFunctor (R := R)).obj
          (op (P.stupidTrunc (ComplexShape.embeddingUpIntGE (k + 1))))).map f))
